notes: Both coders found the same 3 university-layer documents and all 3 were coded delegates. Of 60 matched units, disagreements were: modality (imperative principles coded should vs must, 'may' used as fact coded informs, 'is a violation of' classification coded informs rather than must-not); actor (all vs a named audience when the passage names none; template text addressed to students); policy type (tier-definition sentences P05 vs P09/P41, rationale vs instructor-decision step P41 vs P04, P32 vs P35 for 'AI is not completing students' learning', P59 vs UNCOVERED for the faculty-expertise reminder, P04 vs P56 for the page-level goal sentence). Each was resolved by re-reading the source line and applying the type definition and constant comparison with sibling units; the rationale is in resolution_why. Coder B found 12 units A missed (mostly the planning page's rationale sentences, tier definitions and syllabus list items); 11 were kept and 1 dropped (the sentence 'Written or other work students submit must be the product of their own efforts', which does not mention AI). Coder A found 2 units B missed (consumer-tools data clause, faculty-adapt sentence in the sample-statements page); both kept. One merged A unit (guided approach) was split into permitted-uses (P05) and documentation (P24). Topics were normalised to the starter codebook. Only one UNCOVERED unit remains (faculty expertise reminder); no new types.
